Looking at it again, in past events, Mizuki has run away before,
and we tend to think of running away as a bad thing, but while talking to LUKA-san
and LEN-kun, they realize that running away isn't necessarily bad.
Instead of seeing it as running away, it's more like taking a break or a moment to catch your breath.
I think that was really the core of "Our Survival Struggle."
Personally, if you asked me if I liked school,
since I do this job, I get asked a lot about what I was like as a student.
To be honest, I don't have many good memories of my student days.
Especially in middle school, I was already working in the entertainment industry,
so I often had to leave school early, even though it was during compulsory education.
The teachers didn't look too kindly on it, and the kids around me
could be quite cold. I felt like I didn't have a place in middle school, and I viewed it all quite objectively.
But when I went to work, I felt like I truly loved what I did. I went to school and studied hard because I wanted to be there.
My workplace was the place where I belonged.
That overlaps a bit with Mizuki. I felt like even if things were tough, I'd be okay as long as I had my job.
When I went to high school, it was a performing arts school, so everyone was doing the same kind of work. We thought alike, and that filter was gone, so it was much easier to breathe.
Some people might see "running away" literally as just running away.
But you don't need to listen to those hecklers. You don't have to care
too much about other people's opinions. Including all of that,
I felt like this story really resonated with me and the way Mizuki lives.
Someone wrote that I'm very decisive. That's true.
I figure once I graduate, I'll never see them again anyway.
We have things like LINE and Twitter these days,
but if you just delete them, it's like they never existed. You can just start over.
You can rebuild your relationships from scratch. In my opinion, if it's too painful,
there are options like transferring schools. It's not impossible to reset everything to zero. If you don't stay in touch, the connection just fades.
There are even shrines for cutting ties in Kyoto and places like that.
Before things get too bad, I think it's a good idea to broaden your horizons and look for a place to escape to.
